I've seen this come up over and over again.
Let's look at an example: tariffs being applied for computers.
Let's say you are someone rich enough to be able to build a computer manufacturing firm and you can do it in the USA.
This takes quite a bit of time to actually build, get all the labor, equipment, etc.
So, when would you want to make this investment? When you are 100% sure that the tariffs are here to stay.
Now, since Trump in his first term would tariff things and then throw away the tariffs within a month or two, this would make this a crazy investment.
You would build your computer manufacturing company over a couple of years and by the time you get there, the tariffs would be gone and then you would not be competitive with the offshore manufacturers.
One of the BIG problems with all this tariff talk is a tariff creates an incentive to manufacture / produce here, but the more complex the good, the longer it would take to do so and the more expensive it would be.
It's unclear to me that ANYONE would take the gamble of these tariffs being in place for a multiple year span, hence you don't see anyone making the massive investment to manufacture in the USA. Most of the pro-tariff folks seem to believe you can instantly set up domestic production, but that's 100% not true. It takes a lot of time and a lot of money.
